entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Confucius?
entries.text: Confucius (born 551 BC, died 479 BC) was an important Chinese educator and philosopher. His original name was Kong Qiu or Zhong Ni.
entries.title: Confucius

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Niccolò Machiavelli?
entries.text: Niccolò Machiavelli (3 May 1469 – 21 June 1527) was a Florentine Renaissance man, statesman, and writer. He was a diplomat and government official in the Medici period of the Florentine Republic.
entries.title: Niccolò Machiavelli

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Friedrich Nietzsche?
entries.text: Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche was a German philosopher, writer, and scholar of ancient languages. He was born on 15 October 1844 and died on 25 August 1900.
entries.title: Friedrich Nietzsche

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Thomas Aquinas?
entries.text: St. Thomas Aquinas, (1225 – 7 March 1274) was a Catholic Dominican priest from Italy, saint and philosopher. He was born in Roccasecca, as the son of Count Andulf of Aquino and Countess Theodora of Teano.
entries.title: Thomas Aquinas

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Moses?
entries.text: Moses (Mōše; Ancient Greek: Mωϋσῆς in both the Septuagint and the New Testament; Arabic: موسىٰ, Mūsa) is a person in Abrahamic religions. He was a religious leader, lawgiver, and prophet according to the Hebrew Bible.
entries.title: Moses

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Genghis Khan?
entries.text: Genghis Khan (born Temüjin; c. 1162 – August 1227), also known as Chinggis Khan, was the first ruler of the Mongol Empire, which he created in 1206 in his fatherland in what is now Mongolia.
entries.title: Genghis Khan

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Umar?
entries.text: Umar ibn al-Khattab (Arabic: عُمَر بْن ٱلْخَطَّاب, romanized: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb; c. 582/583 – 644), also spelled Omar, was the second Rashidun caliph, ruling from August 634, when he succeeded Abu Bakr (r. 632–634) as the second caliph, until his assassination in 644.
entries.title: Umar

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Euclid?
entries.text: Euclid of Alexandria (Greek: Εὐκλείδης) (about 325 BC–265 BC) was a Greek mathematician who lived in Alexandria, Egypt and worked at the Library of Alexandria. Little is known about this person, but people think he lived there when Ptolemy I was Pharaoh.
entries.title: Euclid

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Carl Linnaeus?
entries.text: Carl Linnaeus (23 May 1707 – 10 January 1778), also known as Carolus Linnaeus, was a Swedish botanist, physician and zoologist who created the binomial nomenclature. In this system, every kind of animal and plant is given a name consisting of two Latin words, for its genus and species.
entries.title: Carl Linnaeus

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was James Watt?
entries.text: James Watt (19 January 1736 – 25 August 1819) was a Scottish mathematician and engineer. He did not invent the first steam engine, but he did modify it to work better.
entries.title: James Watt

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Francisco de Goya?
entries.text: Francisco José de Goya y Lucientes (30 March 1746 – 30 April 1828) was a Spanish painter. He painted many portraits of the Spanish Royal Family.
entries.title: Francisco de Goya

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Johann Sebastian Bach?
entries.text: Johann Sebastian Bach (31 March 1685 in Eisenach – 28 July 1750 in Leipzig; pronounced BAHK) was a German composer, who was more known as an organist in his time. He lived in the last part of the Baroque period.
entries.title: Johann Sebastian Bach

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Ludwig van Beethoven?
entries.text: Ludwig van Beethoven (baptized 17 December 1770 in Bonn – 26 March 1827 in Vienna; pronounced LUD-vig vahn BAY-TOH-ven) was a German composer. He wrote classical music for the piano, orchestras and different groups of instruments.
entries.title: Ludwig van Beethoven

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Johannes Brahms?
entries.text: Johannes Brahms (7 May 1833 – 3 April 1897) was a famous German composer. He started his career as a pianist.
entries.title: Johannes Brahms

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Giuseppe Verdi?
entries.text: Giuseppe Verdi (born Roncole near Busseto, 9 or 10 October 1813; died Milan 27 January 1901) was an Italian composer of operas.
entries.title: Giuseppe Verdi

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was James Joyce?
entries.text: James Augustine Aloysius Joyce (Irish: Séamus Seoighe) (2 February 1882 – 13 January 1941) was an Irish writer and poet of the modernist movement. He was from Dublin, Ireland.
entries.title: James Joyce

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Franz Kafka?
entries.text: Franz Kafka (born Prague July 3, 1883 – died near Vienna June 3, 1924) was a Czech-born, German-speaking writer. His best known works are The Metamorphosis and the novels The Trial and The Castle.
entries.title: Franz Kafka

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Fundamentalism?
entries.text: Fundamentalism was used at first to describe some people in the Protestant community in the United States in the early 20th century. These people had a set of well-defined ("fundamental") values.
entries.title: Fundamentalism

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Jainism?
entries.text: Jainism is a dharmic religion which originated in ancient India.
entries.title: Jainism

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Behavior?
entries.text: Behavior (or behaviour) is what a person or animal does and how they act. Behaviors may be conscious or unconscious.
entries.title: Behavior

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Communism?
entries.text: Communism is an idea in politics based on equality, that seeks a world without different social class groups. They say that things like factories, tools and farms (the relations of production) are owned by the bourgeoisie.
entries.title: Communism

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is World Health Organization?
entries.text: The World Health Organization (WHO) is part of the United Nations (UN), working on international public health, with its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. The WHO was established by the UN on April 7, 1948.
entries.title: World Health Organization

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Racism?
entries.text: Racism is the belief that one race, culture or tribe is better than others. It means judging or treating people badly for belonging to a certain race or ethnic group.
entries.title: Racism

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Human rights?
entries.text: Human rights are rights and freedoms that all people should have.
entries.title: Human rights

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Poverty?
entries.text: Poverty means not having enough money for basic needs such as food, drinking water, shelter, or toiletries. Many people in different countries live in poverty, especially in developing areas of West and Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, Caribbean and some parts of Asia.
entries.title: Poverty

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Anatomy?
entries.text: Anatomy is the study of the bodies of people and other animals. Anatomy is the study of the inside of the body and outside the body.
entries.title: Anatomy

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Nerve?
entries.text: A nerve is a group of special nerve cells grouped together in parallel. Another word for nerve cell is neuron.
entries.title: Nerve

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Health?
entries.text: Health is a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Physical health is about the body.
entries.title: Health

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Ethanol?
entries.text: Ethanol, also known as ethyl alcohol, grain alcohol or just alcohol, is a flammable, colorless chemical compound whose chemical formula is C2H5OH, also written as C2H6O. It is the active part of alcoholic drinks, which are drunk in most cultures worldwide.
entries.title: Ethanol

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Tuberculosis?
entries.text: Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease caused by bacteria. In the past, people called it consumption or the white death.
entries.title: Tuberculosis

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Biochemistry?
entries.text: Biochemistry is the study of chemical reactions in living beings, and of biological molecules in general. It is important to cell biology and physiology.
entries.title: Biochemistry

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Salt?
entries.text: In chemistry, a salt is any neutral chemical compound made of cations (positive ions) attached to anions (negative ions). The most common example of a salt is sodium chloride, with the chemical formula NaCl - this is the table salt that people use in food.
entries.title: Salt

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Iron?
entries.text: This article is about iron the metal. For the tool called iron, see ironing.
entries.title: Iron

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Analytical chemistry?
entries.text: Analytical chemistry is the part of chemistry that focuses on finding out what a substance is, how much of it there is, and what it is made of. It helps scientists figure out exactly what’s in a sample and in what amounts through analysis.
entries.title: Analytical chemistry

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Snow?
entries.text: Snow is a form of ice. Snow forms when water in the atmosphere becomes frozen.
entries.title: Snow

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Magnet?
entries.text: A magnet is made of magnetic metals such as iron, nickel, or cobalt, and sometimes certain rare earth metals like neodymium. When a magnet goes near one of these magnetic metals or another magnet, and the poles (sides) touching are opposite, it will pull, or attract the other object closer.
entries.title: Magnet

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Pythagorean theorem?
entries.text: In mathematics, the Pythagorean theorem or Pythagoras's theorem is a statement about the sides of a right triangle.
entries.title: Pythagorean theorem

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who is Water?
entries.text: Water (H2O) is a simple chemical compound made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. It is clear, has no taste or smell, and is almost colorless.
entries.title: Water

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Internet?
entries.text: The Internet is the world’s largest global communication network for computers and other devices.
entries.title: Internet

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Nuclear power?
entries.text: Nuclear power is the controlled use of nuclear energy. Nuclear energy can be released by nuclear reactions in a machine called a nuclear reactor.
entries.title: Nuclear power

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Steam engine?
entries.text: A steam engine is an engine that uses steam from boiling water to make it move. The steam pushes on the engine parts to make them move.
entries.title: Steam engine

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Machine gun?
entries.text: A machine gun is a weapon that can fire one bullet after another as long as the trigger is pulled and there are bullets ready to fire. This is called automatic fire.
entries.title: Machine gun

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Art?
entries.text: Art is a creative activity. It produces a product, an object.
entries.title: Art

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Comics?
entries.text: In comics, stories or information are given using pictures, or pictures and words together. A story is told with pictures, mostly in panels.
entries.title: Comics

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Statue of Liberty?
entries.text: The Statue of Liberty (officially named Liberty Enlightening the World and sometimes referred to as Lady Liberty) is a monument symbolising the United States. The statue is placed on Liberty Island, near New York City Harbor.
entries.title: Statue of Liberty

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Television?
entries.text: A television set (also known as a television receiver or televisor or simply a television, TV set, TV receiver or TV) is a machine with a screen or set of lenses. Televisions receive broadcasting signals and change them into pictures and sound.
entries.title: Television

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Hip hop?
entries.text: Hip hop is a type of culture/art style that started in the 1970s in The Bronx. It began in Jamaican American, African American, and Puerto Rican/Hispanic and Latino American urban areas in some of the larger cities of the United States.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Jazz?
entries.text: Jazz is a type of music which was invented in the United States. Jazz music combines African-American music with European music.
entries.title: Jazz

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Piano?
entries.text: The piano is an acoustic, keyboard, stringed and percussive instrument in which the strings are struck by wooden hammers that are coated with a softer material (modern hammers are covered with dense wool felt; some early pianos used leather).
entries.title: Piano

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Iron Age?
entries.text: The Iron Age is the period after the Bronze Age in Europe, Asia, and parts of Africa. Iron production took place in Anatolia at least as early as 1200 BC, with some evidence pointing to even earlier dates.
entries.title: Iron Age

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Asia?
entries.text: Asia is the largest continent on Earth by area and number of people. It is mainly in the northern hemisphere.
entries.title: Asia

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is South America?
entries.text: South America is the continent to the south of North America. These two continents are separated by the Panama Canal.
entries.title: South America

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Istanbul?
entries.text: Istanbul, formerly known as Constantinople, is a mega city that sits in both Europe and Asia, divided by the Bosporus. Although it is the largest city of Turkey, it is not the capital.
entries.title: Istanbul

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Rome?
entries.text: Rome (Latin: Roma) is the capital city of Italy. It is also the capital and largest city in the region of Lazio, and the geographical region of Latium.
entries.title: Rome

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Panama Canal?
entries.text: The Panama Canal is a waterway (a canal) in the country of Panama in Central America, that connects the Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean. Because of the way Panama twists, the entrance to the Pacific Ocean is farther east than the entrance to the Atlantic Ocean.
entries.title: Panama Canal

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Sea of Marmara?
entries.text: The Sea of Marmara, also known as the Sea of Marmora or the Marmara Sea, is the inland sea that connects the Black Sea to the Aegean Sea and separates Turkey's Asian and European parts. The Bosphorus is a strait that connects it to the Black Sea and the Dardanelles to the Aegean.
entries.title: Sea of Marmara

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: The Liao River (simplified Chinese: 辽河; traditional Chinese: 遼河; pinyin: Liáo Hé) is the biggest river in northeastern China (Manchuria). It has a length of 1,390 kilometres (860 mi).

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.title: Almaty

entries.text: Canes Venatici is a constellation in the northern sky. It means "the hunting dogs" in Latin.

entries.text: The Iron Age is the period after the Bronze Age in Europe, Asia, and parts of Africa. Iron production took place in Anatolia at least as early as 1200 BC, with some evidence pointing to even earlier dates. In the Mesopotamian states of Sumer, Akkad and Assyria, the use of iron reaches far back, to perhaps 3000 BC. One of the earliest smelted iron artifacts ever found is a dagger with an iron blade found in a Hattic tomb in Anatolia, dating from 2500 BC. The widespread use of iron weapons which replaced bronze weapons rapidly spread throughout the Near East (North Africa, southwest Asia) by the beginning of the 1st millennium BC. Before this time, people used bronze or flint tools and pottery. They farmed, and lived in communities. Most of Europe, Africa and Asia reached the Iron Age by 500 BC. It is a period of prehistory because, though iron and steel continue to be important even today, the "Iron Age" is defined as ending when people began to write their history. Iron ore is easy to find, and some iron is a Native metal but iron is hard to make into tools. It melts at a higher temperature than bronze. When blacksmiths learned how to make iron tools, they were able to make many of them. With more and better tools, people could do more. For example, more people could own a metal plough. They could farm their fields better and grow more crops. Some people invented coins to help buy and sell their crops and their iron tools. Bronze weapons and armor were no match for those mad
entries.title: Iron Age

entries.text: Jainism is a dharmic religion which originated in ancient India. It teaches that "all the events in the universe are self-caused, random, fixed and are independent of previous events or external causes or god": Jain philosophy is the oldest philosophy of India that distinguishes body (matter) from the soul (awareness) completely. It teaches that the universe is eternal and that every living being has a soul which has the power to become all-knowing (observer of all the random events). A soul which has triumphed (prevailed, won) over its inner enemies like attachment, greed, pride, etc. is called jina which means conqueror or victor (over ignorance). The holy book of Jainism is Pravachansara.
entries.title: Jainism

entries.text: In history and politics, a favourite was the intimate companion of a ruler or other important person. In post-classical and early-modern Europe, among other times and places, the term was used of individuals delegated significant political power by a ruler. It was especially a phenomenon of the 16th and 17th centuries, when government had become too complex for many hereditary rulers with no great interest in or talent for it, and political institutions were still evolving. From 1600 to 1660 there were particular successions of all-powerful minister-favourites in much of Europe, particularly in Spain, England, France and Sweden.
entries.title: Favourite

entries.text: In audio signal processing and acoustics, an echo is a reflection of sound that arrives at the listener with a delay after the direct sound. The delay is directly proportional to the distance of the reflecting surface from the source and the listener. Typical examples are the echo produced by the bottom of a well, a building, or the walls of enclosed and empty rooms.
entries.title: Echo
